newsitem.title: INDIA: U.N. official urges balanced outcome on WTO issues.
newsitem.headline: U.N. official urges balanced outcome on WTO issues.

text.p: Countries must work for a balanced outcome on trade and investment issues before the World Trade Organisation (WTO), Ruben Ricupero, secretary general of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), said on Monday.
"In terms of Multilateral Agreement on Investment (MAI) I would say the goal should be to have a balanced outcome," he told a business meeting.
The first ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation is due to be held in Singapore in December.

Industrialised countries want to broaden the WTO canvas to include items like MIA, labour standards and environment. The developing nations say they need time before they can join the other nations on fresh binding multilateral rules.
Parminder Singh, chairman of Ranbaxy Laboratories, said the UNCTAD platform could be used to discuss emerging trade and investment issues.
"We feel that the MAI cannot ask for commitments that will contravene or undermine promises made in the GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) final act," Singh said.
Ricupero said while WTO was a contractual agency, UNCTAD does not negotiate rules. "Our role is more of a prenegotiation phase and also practical application of the results of the negotiations."
Ricupero said in recent years most of the flows of foreign direct investment were taking place among industrialised countries, with the least developed ones getting very little.
He said with the liberalisation of the economy there was a close relationship between trade and foreign direct investment.
Ricupero said in the next few years India would become one of the largest and fastest growing markets of the world.
